sections.section_title: Paul's Address to the Crowd in Hebrew
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes Paul's opening address from the barracks steps in Hebrew (or Aramaic), producing a deeper silence from the crowd.

sections.section_title: Paul's Jewish Credentials and Former Persecution
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents Paul's recitation of his Jewish pedigree -- born in Tarsus, raised in Jerusalem, trained under Gamaliel, zealous for God -- and his former life as a persecutor of the Way, imprisoning and delivering men and women to death.

The neutral reading presents Paul's account of his encounter with a great light from heaven near Damascus, the voice identifying itself as Jesus of Nazareth whom Paul was persecuting, and Paul's resulting blindness and helplessness.

The neutral reading describes Ananias as a devout Torah-observant man who restored Paul's sight and delivered the commission: Paul is appointed to know God's will, see the Righteous One, hear his voice, and be a witness to all people, with the command to rise, be baptized, wash away sins, and call on the Lord's name.

sections.section_title: The Temple Vision and Commission to the Gentiles
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes Paul's vision in the Jerusalem temple where the Lord commanded him to leave Jerusalem quickly because the people would not accept his testimony, and the divine commission sending him far away to the Gentiles.
The neutral reading notes the crowd's violent eruption the moment Paul spoke the word 'Gentiles,' revealing the precise theological boundary the audience would not cross.

sections.section_title: Roman Citizenship and Its Legal Implications
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the tribune's order to examine Paul by flogging, Paul's revelation of his Roman citizenship before the flogging began, and the reversal of power dynamics as the tribune becomes afraid upon learning Paul is a citizen by birth.
The neutral reading describes the tribune's decision to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin to determine the actual nature of the accusation against him.
